text.p: DC International Ltd said on Tuesday it had completed negotiations to buy Radisson Hotels Pty Ltd for A$15.1 million, to be funded by an A$11.9 million rights issue.

DCI said it would make a non-renounnceable rights issue with an entitlement of nine new shares for every ten shares held at a price of 23 cents per share and a placement of 7.2 million shares to clients of SBC Warburg, also at 23 cents per share.

Provision will also be made form any shortfall to the rights issue for a "top-up" facility at the same prices for shareholders who would, after taking up their rights entitlements, have shareholdings of less than 10,000 shares.
DCI said Radisson was a hotel operator focusing on four and five star hotels, owned by its management team, a former director and an Indonesian corporation.
Founded in 1987, it operates under a franchise for Australasia and the South West Pacific and with non-exclusive but preferred status in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.
The franchisor is Radisson Hotels International Inc, owned by Carlson Companies Inc of the United States.
DCI said it would pay A$11.3 million in cash and issue shares to the value of A$3.8 million.
DCI said it would continue to own and operate its architectural and design business Davenport Campbell and also intended to establish a funds management business to develop hotel investment products.
